children.text: Pūrvapakṣaḥ:
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrvapakṣa</s> (the opponent's position):

children.text: yathā sadasatām naiva $ viśeṣo 'sti nijātmani &
children.translated_text: Just as there is no distinction whatsoever in the intrinsic nature of existent and non-existent things,

children.text: jadājaḍānām apy evaṃ % nāsty asāv iti niścayaḥ || 01 ||
children.translated_text: so too there is certainly no such [distinction] between the inert (<s>jaḍa</s>) and the non-inert (<s>ajaḍa</s>). // <s>UtAjp</s> 1 //

children.text: Vṛ: vijñānasantānavādināṃ mate sarveṣāṃ bhāvānāṃ kṣaṇikatvāt svalakṣaṇātmake prātisvike svarūpe viśeṣābhāvaḥ saṃtānina ekasyānusaṃdhātur anabhyupagatatvāt | evaṃ cetanācetanānām api svātmani nirviśeṣatvam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: In the view of the <s>vijñānasantānavādin</s> (proponent of the consciousness-stream), since all entities are momentary (<s>kṣaṇika</s>), there is no distinction in their own individual nature, which consists of unique particulars (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), because no single unifying cognizer (<s>anusaṃdhātṛ</s>) who persists through the stream (<s>saṃtānin</s>) is accepted. In this way, there is also no differentiation in their own nature between the sentient (<s>cetana</s>) and the insentient (<s>acetana</s>).

children.text: prakhyopākhyā ca sattā yad $ yad asattā viparyayaḥ &
naitat svarūpaṃ spṛśati % vastuno jñātṛgāmy adaḥ || 02 ||
children.translated_text: This does not touch the intrinsic nature of the real thing — that [manifestation and denomination] pertains to the knower (<s>jñātṛ</s>). // <s>UtAjp</s> 2 //
<s>Prakhyā</s> (manifestation) and <s>upākhyā</s> (denomination) constitute existence; their opposite is non-existence.

children.text: Vṛ: prakāśavimarśalakṣaṇābhyāṃ prakhyopākhyābhyāṃ tadabhāvena ca bhāvānāṃ sadasattayor vyavasthāpayitum iṣṭayor api vastunaḥ svarūpasparśābhāvaḥ, yatas tatprakhyādi jñātur dharmas tatas tatsvarūpavyavasthānābhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: Even though the existence and non-existence of entities are sought to be established through <s>prakhyā</s> (manifestation) and <s>upākhyā</s> (denomination), characterized as <s>prakāśa</s> (light) and <s>vimarśa</s> (reflective awareness), and through their absence — there is no contact with the intrinsic nature of the real thing, because those [qualities] such as manifestation are properties of the knower (<s>jñātṛ</s>); therefore, the establishment of the thing's own nature [through them] is impossible.

children.text: prakhyopākhyāviṣayatāpy $ arthasyātmā na yujyate &
parāpekṣitayā naika- % rūpatve sattvalaṅghanāt || 03 ||
children.translated_text: because, being dependent on another, [that objecthood] would violate [the thing's] unitary nature and thus transgress [its] existence (<s>sattva</s>). // <s>UtAjp</s> 3 //
Even being an object of <s>prakhyā</s> (manifestation) and <s>upākhyā</s> (denomination) cannot be the essential nature of a thing,

children.text: Vṛ: na ca prakhyādiviṣayatve 'pi padārthasvarūpatopapadyate paraprakāśādhīnatvāt tasya | kiṃ cānekākāratve 'pi vastusattāyā apratiṣṭhānāt | tasmād anyonyaṃ vastutadabhāvayor nirviśeṣatvam |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: Nor is [this objecthood] established as the essential nature of the entity even when it is an object of manifestation and the rest, because that [objecthood] is dependent on the illumination by another. Moreover, because the reality (<s>vastusattā</s>) of the thing has no stable ground even in [its] manifold forms. Therefore, there is mutual non-differentiation between a real thing and its absence.

children.text: mā bhūd viśeṣaḥ prakhyādi- $ bhāvābhāvau tataḥ punaḥ &
siddhyaty eva viśeṣo 'tra % tāvatā ca prayojanam || 04 ||
children.translated_text: from that, a distinction is indeed established here, and that much serves the purpose. // <s>UtAjp</s> 4 //
Let there be no [intrinsic] distinction; still, the presence and absence of <s>prakhyā</s> (manifestation) and the rest —

children.text: Vṛ: nirviśeṣatvābhyupagame 'pi sadasator vastunoḥ prakhyādi bhāvābhāvāv avikalāv eva tad avalambya punar viśeṣavattvasya siddheḥ, tataḥ sākalyena bhāveṣv arthakriyāpi siddhyed eva ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: Even if the non-differentiation of the existent and non-existent real things is accepted, the presence and absence of manifestation (<s>prakhyā</s>) and the rest remain fully intact; relying on that, the possession of distinction is established again. From that, <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy) too would be established in all entities.

children.text: evam apy avabhāsānu- $ ṣaktā sattocitā bhavet &
tadapekṣāṃ vinā bhāvā- % bhāvayor aviśiṣṭatā || 05 ||
children.translated_text: without dependence on that [manifestation], there would be no differentiation between existence and non-existence. // <s>UtAjp</s> 5 //
Even so, existence would properly belong only to that which is conjoined with manifestation (<s>avabhāsa</s>);

children.text: Vṛ: itthaṃ ca vastusattāyāḥ prakāśalagnāyā evaucityaṃ prakāśamānatālakṣaṇaṃ saṃbhāvyate 'nyathā saṃvidanuṣaṅgaṃ vinā sadasator anyonyanirapekṣatvāt svasvarūpaniṣṭhayor viśeṣānupapatteḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: And thus, the fitness of the reality of a thing is conceivable only as having the character of being-manifested, since it clings to <s>prakāśa</s> (light/manifestation). Otherwise, without connection to <s>saṃvid</s> (consciousness), the existent and the non-existent, being mutually independent and each abiding in its own nature alone, would admit of no differentiation.

children.text: kathaṃ syād aviśeṣo 'tra $ yāvatārthakriyāṃ hi san &
kuryān nānyas tathāpy artho % nirviśeṣo nijātmani || 06 ||
children.translated_text: produces <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy), and the other does not — yet even so, the thing is without distinction in its own nature. // <s>UtAjp</s> 6 //
How could there be no distinction here? For the existent

children.text: Vṛ: yasmāt sata eva vastuno 'rthakriyākāritvam asatas tadabhāva iti katham aviśiṣṭatvam arthakriyayaiva tadbhāvopapādanāt, ity ākṣepaḥ | tatrāha tathāpy arthakriyāyās tattatpramātradhīnatayā naisargikatvābhāvād vinā saṃvidāśrayatām arthasya svātmani viśeṣādhāyaktvāsiddheḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: Since only a real, existent thing has the capacity for <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy), and the non-existent lacks it — how can there be non-differentiation? [The opponent argues that] their distinction is established precisely by <s>arthakriyā</s> itself. This is the objection. To that, [the author] replies: even so, since <s>arthakriyā</s> is dependent on particular knowers (<s>pramātṛ</s>) and thus lacks an innate [inherent] character, without the thing's taking refuge in <s>saṃvid</s> (consciousness), its capacity to ground any distinction in its own nature is not established.

children.text: evam arthakriyābhāso- $ pādhisaṃbhedam āgataḥ &
sann arthaḥ syāt svarūpeṇa % nāsatas tu viśiṣyate || 07 ||
children.translated_text: would possess reality [only] in that form, but would not be distinguished from a non-existent [thing] in its own intrinsic nature. // <s>UtAjp</s> 7 //
Thus, an existent thing, having merged with the adventitious conditions (<s>upādhi</s>) of the appearances (<s>ābhāsa</s>) of <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy),

children.text: Vṛ: uktaprakāreṇa saṃvidy apratiṣṭhānād arthakriyākāribhis tattadābhāsopādhibhiḥ saṃbhinnasyārthasyārthasvarūpeṇa sattāsaṃoattāv api punar asato 'rthād viśeṣo na siddhyet ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: In the manner described, since [the thing's reality] has no stable ground in <s>saṃvid</s> (consciousness), the thing — though merged with the various adventitious conditions (<s>upādhi</s>) of appearances that are causally efficacious — even if it possesses existence in its nature as a thing, still no distinction from a non-existent thing could be established.

children.text: tatrāpy arthakriyā siddha- $ sattākārthe na varṇitā &
samam evānayos tena % pratiṣṭhā saṃvidāśrayā || 08 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, the ground of both [existence and non-existence] equally is dependence on <s>saṃvid</s> (consciousness). // <s>UtAjp</s> 8 //
Moreover, <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy) is not [validly] attributed to a thing whose existence is already established [independently];

children.text: Vṛ: tayor ubhayoḥ sadasator madhye 'pi prāgasiddhe 'rthe 'rthakriyāyā avyavasthitatvāt, atha ca pūrvasiddhe 'rthe tatsiddher nārthakriyaiva vastvātmā; tasmād bhāvābhāvayor akramam eva saṃvidadhīnaiva siddhis tanniṣṭhatvād eva bhāvavyavasthitīnām ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: Even between the two — existent and non-existent — <s>arthakriyā</s> is not stably established for a thing not previously established; and if the thing is already established prior [to causal efficacy], then <s>arthakriyā</s> itself is not the essence of the real thing. Therefore, the establishment of both existence and non-existence depends solely on <s>saṃvid</s> (consciousness), without sequence, since the determinations of entities are grounded in that [consciousness] alone.

children.text: saṃvid apy aparāmarśa- $ rūpā cet tad asāv api &
abhāvena jaḍenātha % tulyaiva prāgvad ātmani || 09 ||
children.translated_text: would be entirely equal to the non-existent and to the inert (<s>jaḍa</s>) in its own nature, just as before. // <s>UtAjp</s> 9 //
If <s>saṃvid</s> (consciousness) too is of the nature of non-reflective-awareness (<s>aparāmarśa</s>), then it also

children.text: Vṛ: nirvimarśasya prakāśasyāpi sphaṭikādivad viśvāvabhāsane 'py asvatantratvāt svātmany asatā jaḍena ca bhāvena sādṛśyam eva syāt parasparavṛttaparijñāne 'nelamūkaprāyatvāt, etena śāntabrahmavādanirāsaḥ kaṭākṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: Even <s>prakāśa</s> (light) devoid of <s>vimarśa</s> (reflective self-awareness), though it may manifest the entire universe like a crystal and the like, would, due to its lack of autonomy, be identical in its own nature with the non-existent and the inert — because in the mutual cognition [of things], it would be like one who is blind and mute. By this, the doctrine of quiescent <s>Brahman</s> (<s>śāntabrahmavāda</s>) is also glanced at [i.e., refuted in passing].

children.text: saivaṃ bhūtātmanā svenāpy $ alabdhapariniṣṭhitiḥ &
katham anyasya bhāvasya % pratiṣṭhāspadatām iyāt || 10 ||
children.translated_text: how could [consciousness] attain the status of being the foundation of another entity? (10)
That [consciousness], being of such a nature, would not attain stable establishment even through its own self;

children.text: Vṛ: nirvimarśā saṃvit svato ' labdhasattākā paraṃ vyavasthāpayituṃ nālaṃ gaganakusumam iva saurabhādijanane ||
children.translated_text: Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>): Awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>) devoid of reflective cognition (<s>vimarśa</s>), being of inherently unestablished existence, is unable to establish another [entity] — just as a sky-flower [cannot] produce fragrance and so on.

children.text: idam ity ucitaḥ saṃvit $ prakāśe 'nyasya vastunaḥ &
pratiṣṭhātmakatāṃ gacched % aham ity ātmanā punaḥ || 11 ||
children.translated_text: but it would attain the nature of being a foundation through the self-form 'I.' (11)
In the illumination of another object, 'this' is the appropriate [mode of] awareness;

children.text: Vṛ: bhinnaṃ vastu idaṃtāvimarśena prakāśanārhaṃ sat punar ahaṃtātmanā vyavasthām iyāt | saṃvid eva viśvasphurattāmayī svasvātantryād eva vicitrārthātmanāvibhinnaprakāśamayena prasphurantī viśvajīvitaṃ, tad ahaṃtāviśrāntiṃ vinā svato 'siddhaṃ kathaṃ vyavahāryaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: Commentary: A separate object, when worthy of illumination through the reflective cognition of 'this-ness' (<s>idaṃtā</s>), would attain [its] establishment through the self-form of 'I-ness' (<s>ahaṃtā</s>). Awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>) itself, consisting of the manifestation of the universe, shining forth by its own sovereignty (<s>svātantrya</s>) alone, as an undifferentiated mass of illumination having the nature of diverse objects — [this] is the life of the universe; without repose in that 'I-ness,' being inherently unestablished, how could it become the object of ordinary transactions?

children.text: vyatireketarābhyām hi $ niścayo 'nyajaḍātmanoḥ &
vyavasthitiḥ pratiṣṭhā ca % siddhir nirvṛttir ucyate || 12 ||
children.translated_text: their establishment, foundation, and accomplishment (<s>siddhi</s>), i.e., completion — is declared. (12)
For by [the methods of] co-presence (<s>anvaya</s>) and co-absence (<s>vyatireka</s>), the determination of the other [i.e., the inert] and the non-inert (<s>ajaḍa</s>),

children.text: Vṛ: jñātari vyavasthitatve san jaḍo 'nyathāsan, svātmānyasaṃrambhatve svaprakāśatvaṃ tadabhāve nāstīty anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ hi svaparatvaniścayaḥ, sa ca vyavasthāpratiṣṭhādiśabdair ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Commentary: When [an object is] established in the knower, it exists as inert; otherwise it does not [exist]. When there is the activity of self and other [in consciousness], self-luminosity is [present]; in its absence, it is not — thus by <s>anvaya</s> (co-presence) and <s>vyatireka</s> (co-absence), the determination of self and other [is made]; and that is expressed by the words 'establishment,' 'foundation,' and the like.

children.text: evam ātmany asatkalpāḥ $ prakāśasyaiva santy amī &
jaḍāḥ prakāśa evāsti % svātmanaḥ svaparātmabhiḥ || 13 ||
children.translated_text: [all] inert [things] exist as illumination itself, [constituted] by the self- and other-forms of its own nature. (13)
Thus, in the Self, these [entities], which are virtually non-existent, belong to illumination (<s>prakāśa</s>) alone;

children.text: Vṛ: itthaṃ jaḍabhāvānāṃ saṃvidviśrāntiṃ vināsatkalpatvāt svātmany asatsvabhāvānāṃ jñātuḥ prakāśasvabhāvasya saṃbandhitayaiva sattvaṃ, tasmāt saṃvitprakāśa eva svātmocchalattayā svamāyāśaktyullāsite viśvavaicitrye jaḍājaḍabhāvarāśidvayena vedyavedakātmakena svarūpānatiriktenātirikteneva prashpuret, -- iti svātantryavādasya pronmīlanaṃ sūcitavān ācāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Commentary: Thus, since inert entities are virtually non-existent (<s>asatkalpa</s>) without reposing in awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>), having an unreal nature in their own self — their existence is only as [entities] related to the knower whose nature is illumination (<s>prakāśa</s>). Therefore, it is in the illumination of awareness itself that, as the effulgence of its own nature, in the variegation of the universe that is displayed by the play of its own <s>Māyā</s>-power — [the universe] would shine forth through the two masses of inert and non-inert entities, of the nature of the known and the knower, as though distinct [yet] not distinct from its own nature — thus the master has indicated the opening forth of the doctrine of sovereignty (<s>svātantryavāda</s>).

children.text: na caivānubhavo 'py asti $ bhinnābhinnaviniścayam &
muktvānvayasya prakāśasya % vimarśarahitātmanaḥ || 14 ||
children.translated_text: apart from the reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>) of illumination that pervades [all experiences] — [illumination that is] devoid of reflective cognition [on its own, would be inert]. (14)
Moreover, there is no experience whatsoever that could determine [anything as] separate or non-separate,

children.text: Vṛ: saṃyojanaviyojanātmakaṃ svātantryaṃ vihāya sato jaḍaprakāśasya naiva saṃrambhātmānubhavo nirvimarśātmakatvāt | etad eva hi pratyavamarśasya māhātmyaṃ yad viśvaṃ svātmaikyenāntaḥsthitaṃ bahiridaṃtayodbhāsayan udbhāsyamānam api punaḥ pūrṇāhaṃtāviśrāntyabhedam āpādayet ||
children.translated_text: Commentary: Apart from sovereignty (<s>svātantrya</s>) consisting of conjunction and disjunction, inert illumination, [even when] existent, simply has no experience [of itself] as self-activity — because of being devoid of reflective cognition (<s>vimarśa</s>). This indeed is the greatness of reflective awareness (<s>pratyavamarśa</s>): that the universe, internally abiding in unity with the Self, while manifesting it externally as 'this,' would [re]integrate even the manifested [universe] into the non-difference of repose in full 'I-ness' (<s>pūrṇāhaṃtā</s>).

children.text: idam ity asya vicchinna- $ vimarśasya kṛtārthatā &
yā svasvarūpe viśrāntir % vimarśaḥ so 'ham ity ayam || 15 ||
children.translated_text: that repose in [awareness's] own nature is the reflective cognition 'I am this.' (15)
The purpose served by [the cognition] 'this' — of that whose reflective cognition is delimited —

children.text: Vṛ: idam iti vicchinnatayā vimṛśyasyāsya jaḍasya yā saṃvitsvarūpaviśrāntilakṣaṇā kṛtārthatā so 'yam aham eva tattadbhāvavaicitryātmanā prakāśe iti caitanyaprakāśatādātmyād ahaṃpratyavamarṣātmā jīvitasthānīyaḥ, yadāśrayāj jaḍam api vastu vimraṣṭṛsvabhāvapramātraikyād ahaṃbhāvaviśrānter ajaḍatvam āyāti | ajaḍāś ca vastutaḥ parapramātrekasvabhāvāḥ, -- ity advaito 'jaḍapramātṛbhāva eva sarvataḥ pāripūrṇyena vijṛmbhate iti tātparyam ||
children.translated_text: Commentary: Of this inert [entity] that is reflectively cognized in a delimited manner as 'this' — the fulfillment of purpose characterized by repose in the nature of awareness itself — that is 'I am indeed this [very universe], shining in the variegation of such-and-such states of being' — this reflective self-awareness of 'I' (<s>ahaṃpratyavamarṣa</s>), by virtue of its identity with the illumination of consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>), holds the place of life-breath. By dependence upon this [I-awareness], even an inert object attains non-inertness through unity with the cognizer whose nature is reflective consciousness — [through] repose in 'I-ness' (<s>ahaṃbhāva</s>). And [all entities,] in reality, are of one nature with the other/supreme cognizer — thus the purport is that the non-dual state of the non-inert cognizer (<s>ajaḍapramātṛbhāva</s>) alone manifests everywhere in complete fullness.

children.text: dvidhā sa eṣa evātmā $ mito 'parimitas tathā &
prāṇādinā niruddho 'ṇuḥ % paramātmā tv akhaṇḍitaḥ || 16 ||
children.translated_text: contracted by <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) and the rest, [it is] atomic (<s>aṇu</s>); but the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) is undivided. (16)
This same Self is twofold: limited and unlimited;

children.text: Vṛ: sa eva saṃvidātmā parameśvaraḥ svecchayā viśvakrīḍollilāsayiṣāyāṃ prāṇādyātmatām avabhāsya tatpramātṛtvena saṃkucitībhūya jīvatām eti, prāṇādyaniruddhas tu viśvanirbharitātmatayā pūrṇaḥ svatantraś cidātmaiveti parimitāparimitatvena dvividhatvam ||
children.translated_text: Commentary: That same Self whose nature is awareness — the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) — by His own will, desiring to play the game of universal creation, manifesting [Himself] as the nature of <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest, becoming contracted as [a limited] cognizer, becomes a <s>jīva</s> (individual soul). But unobstructed by <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest, by virtue of being full with the nature of containing the universe, [He is] complete, sovereign — consciousness itself. Thus the twofold nature [arises] as limited and unlimited.

children.text: ubhayo 'py eṣa paryanta- $ bhūmiḥ sarvārthasaṃvidām &
eka evānusandhānād % ato 'nyo nopapadyate || 17 ||
children.translated_text: [it is] one alone, from [the evidence of] continuous recollection (<s>anusandhāna</s>) — therefore no other [self] is tenable. (17)
In both [forms], this [Self] is the ultimate ground of all cognitions of objects;

children.text: Vṛ: dvividhasyāpy asya prakāśātmanaḥ samastabhāvābhāvātmikānām arthasaṃvidāṃ viśrāntyāspadatvam | sa ca paurvāparyānusaṃdhātṛtayā saṃvinmātrasphurattaikarūpa eva yasmād ato bhedānupapattiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Commentary: Even of this twofold [Self] whose nature is illumination, [it is] the resting place of all cognitions of objects — [cognitions] whose nature consists of all entities and non-entities. And that [Self], being the one who connects [experiences in their] earlier and later [sequence] (<s>paurvāparyānusaṃdhātṛ</s>), is of one form as the mere flash of awareness — because of this, difference is untenable.

children.text: na cāpy avyatirekātma- $ vimarśātmany ahaṃvidi &
bhāti paryantavartinyāṃ % bhāsanād adhikaṃ jaḍam || 18 ||
children.translated_text: (verse 18cd) it shines at the ultimate boundary — beyond [its] shining, the inert [has no existence].
And in this knower of 'I' (<s>ahaṃvid</s>), whose reflective cognition has the nature of non-difference —

children.text: Vṛ: na ca viśvābhinnapratyavamarśasvarūpe 'haṃprakāśe sarvajñānaviśrāntibhūmau tatprakāśādhikyena jaḍasya sattā, tasya saṃvitprakāśād bhedābhedavikalpair upahatatvāt, ata eka evājaḍapramātā svasvātantryeṇa svābhinnaṃ bhāvajātaṃ svātmany evodbhāsayan vilāpayāṃś cāpracyutasvātmasthitiḥ prasphuratītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And in the I-light (<s>ahaṃprakāśa</s>), whose nature is the reflective awareness (<s>pratyavamarśa</s>) undifferentiated from the universe — the ground of repose of all cognitions — the existence of the inert through a predominance of that light is [impossible], since the inert is impaired by the concepts of difference and non-difference from the light of consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>). Therefore, the meaning is: one single non-inert knower (<s>ajaḍapramātṛ</s>), by his own autonomy (<s>svāsvātantrya</s>), manifesting the totality of entities — not different from himself — in his own self alone, and dissolving [them], shines forth without falling from his own self-establishment.

children.text: na siddho 'prathanād eva $ jñānādisamavāyy api &
tat prāṇādi prameyaṃ syān % na pramātānyato bhramāt || 19 ||
children.translated_text: (verse 19cd) that [entity associated with] <s>prāṇa</s> etc. would be an object of knowledge (<s>prameya</s>), not a knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>) — otherwise, due to error.
(verse 19ab) [A limited knower] is not established, due to mere non-manifestation [of his nature] — even though conjoined with knowledge and such [qualities],

children.text: Vṛ: jñānādiguṇaiḥ samaveto 'pi parimitapramātā vimarśavaidhuryād eva na siddhyati nirvimarśatve jāḍyaprasaṅgāt, tasmād vyavacchinnāṃ bhrāntim āśritya prāṇapuryaṣṭakamātur vedyatvaṃ syān na paramārthapramātṛbhāvaḥ saṃbhāvyate ||
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Even though conjoined with the qualities of knowledge etc., a limited knower (<s>parimita-pramātṛ</s>) is not established precisely due to the absence of reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>), since in the absence of <s>vimarśa</s> there would be the absurd consequence of inertness (<s>jāḍya</s>). Therefore, by resorting to a delimited error (<s>bhrānti</s>), the <s>prāṇa</s>-<s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (subtle body)-based entity's status would be that of a knowable object — the ultimate status of a true knower is not to be expected [for it].

children.text: yady apy arthasthitiḥ prāṇa- $ puryaṣṭakaniyantrite &
jīve niruddhā tatrāpi % paramātmani sā sthitā || 20 ||
children.translated_text: (verse 20cd) even there, it abides in the Supreme Self (<s>paramātman</s>).
(verse 20ab) Even though the stability of objects is governed in the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) bound by <s>prāṇa</s> and the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>),

children.text: Vṛ: māyāvyavahārātmani lokayātrāyāṃ yady api prāṇādi saṃkocavati jīve sarveṣāṃ bāhyābhyantarāṇāṃ viṣayāṇāṃ vyavasthitir niyantritā tathāpi saṃkucitātmani tatra mitapramātari saṃkocāpahastanena parapramātrekātmatayā śivātmany eva sā tiṣṭhati prāṇādeś citprakāśād avyatirekitvāt, śivasyaiva svecchayā samullāsitāyāḥ paśubhūmikāyā grahaṇenāṇubhāvābhyupagamāt ||
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] In the realm of conventional transactions (<s>māyā-vyavahāra</s>), even though the establishment of all external and internal objects is governed in the <s>jīva</s> contracted by <s>prāṇa</s> etc., nevertheless, in that contracted self — that limited knower — by the removal of contraction, [that stability] abides precisely in <s>Śiva</s>'s self as one with the Supreme Knower (<s>parapramātṛ</s>), since <s>prāṇa</s> etc. are not different from the light of consciousness (<s>citprakāśa</s>); and because, by <s>Śiva</s>'s own will, having assumed the level of a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>), there is acceptance of the state of a limited being (<s>aṇubhāva</s>).

children.text: tadātmanaiva tasya syāt $ kathaṃ prāṇena yantraṇā &
sādhitā pratyabhijñāyām % akhyāter jīvatā param || 21 ||
children.translated_text: (verse 21cd) It has been established in the <s>Pratyabhijñā</s> [treatise] that the state of being a <s>jīva</s> is nothing but non-recognition (<s>akhyāti</s>).
(verse 21ab) For that which is of His very nature, how could there be constraint by <s>prāṇa</s>?

children.text: Vṛ: tasmād vastutaḥ śivasvabhāvābhinnena prāṇādipramātrā saṃkucitaśuktikena katham anavacchinnaprakāśānandamayapūrṇāhaṃtāsphurattātmanaḥ śivasyāvabhāsananirodhaḥ syāt tathātve tasya svayaṃ sthātum aśakyatvāt kevalam aparicchinnasvaśaktivikāsasyāprathanam eva bandhakatvaparyāyaṃ jīvatvaṃ, tasya ceśvarapratyabhijñāyāṃ śāstre savistaraṃ nirṇītatvād iti tata eva vivecyam ||
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, in reality, how could there be a concealment of the manifestation of <s>Śiva</s> — whose nature is the pulsation (<s>sphurattā</s>) of full I-consciousness (<s>pūrṇāhaṃtā</s>) of unlimited light and bliss — by a knower such as <s>prāṇa</s> etc., who is a contracted shell, not different in nature from <s>Śiva</s>? For in that case, he would be unable to exist by himself. Rather, the mere non-manifestation (<s>aprathana</s>) of the expansion of his own undivided power is what is synonymous with bondage — the state of being a <s>jīva</s>. And since this has been thoroughly determined in the <s>Īśvarapratyabhijñā</s> treatise, it should be examined from that [work].

children.text: nārthavyavasthā prāṇādāv $ ahaṃbhāvanirodhataḥ &
prakāśasyātmaviśrāntir % ahaṃbhāvo hi kīrtitaḥ || 22 ||
children.translated_text: (verse 22cd) for the self-repose (<s>ātmaviśrānti</s>) of light (<s>prakāśa</s>) is declared to be I-consciousness.
(verse 22ab) There is no stability of objects in <s>prāṇa</s> etc., due to the cessation of I-consciousness (<s>ahaṃbhāva</s>) —

children.text: uktā saiva ca viśrāntiḥ $ sarvāpekṣānirodhataḥ &
svātantryam atha kartṛtvaṃ % mukhyam īśvaratāpi ca || 23 ||
children.translated_text: (verse 23cd) to be autonomy (<s>svātantrya</s>), and also primary agency (<s>kartṛtva</s>), and also sovereignty (<s>īśvaratā</s>).
(verse 23ab) And that very repose is said, due to the cessation of all dependence [on other factors],

children.text: Vṛ: prāṇādau parimitapramātrāspade jaḍe svātmamātrasphurattātmanaḥ parāmarśasya nirodhān naiva vastuvyavasthā tasyāḥ saṃvinniṣṭhatvāt, yato yā saṃvidaḥ svātmamātraviśrāntiḥ sa eva pūrṇāhaṃtāvimarśasvabhāvo 'haṃbhāvo 'rthavyavasthāpako gīyate | saiva viśvabhāvānāṃ paryantapratiṣṭhābhūmikatvād viśrāntiḥ, viśvaprasaraṇe svavyatiriktasāmagrīnirapekṣatvāt svātantryaṃ, tad eva kartṛtvaṃ mukhyam aiśvaryam apy āgameṣūdghoṣyate ||
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] In <s>prāṇa</s> etc. — the seat of the limited knower, which is inert — since the reflective awareness (<s>parāmarśa</s>) whose nature is the pulsation of one's own self alone is suppressed, there can be no stability of objects, since that [stability] depends on consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>). For what is declared to be I-consciousness (<s>ahaṃbhāva</s>) — whose nature is the reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>) of full I-ness (<s>pūrṇāhaṃtā</s>) — that is the self-repose of consciousness in its own self alone, establishing objects. That very [I-consciousness], being the ground of final establishment for all world-entities, is repose (<s>viśrānti</s>); being independent of any external aggregate for the emanation of the universe, it is autonomy (<s>svātantrya</s>); and that same [thing] is proclaimed in the scriptures (<s>āgama</s>) to be primary agency (<s>kartṛtva</s>) and also sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>).

children.text: māyābhidās tacchakter eva $ cānyāprasiddhitaḥ &
tadakhyātimayaṃ hy etaj % jagannirmātṛteśitā || 24 ||
children.translated_text: (verse 24cd) and because nothing else is established [as its cause] — this world, composed of non-recognition (<s>akhyāti</s>), is the sovereignty of its creator.
(verse 24ab) And because the power called <s>Māyā</s> belongs to that very [<s>Śiva</s>'s] <s>Śakti</s>,

children.text: Vṛ: māyā nāma śaktiḥ śivasya śaktimato 'vyatirekiṇī svarūpagopanātmikā krīḍā, tannimittād eva yasmād akhyātimayam etad viśvaṃ bhāsate vyatiriktakāraṇasya bhedābhedavikalpopahatatvenāprasiddhatvāt, tasmād viśvābhāsānāṃ nirmātṛtvam īśvaratvam ||
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] <s>Māyā</s> is the power of <s>Śiva</s>, not different from the possessor of power — [it is his] play (<s>krīḍā</s>) whose nature is the concealment of his own nature. Since precisely because of that [<s>Māyā</s>], this universe appears as composed of non-recognition — because a separate cause is not established, being impaired by the concepts of difference and non-difference — therefore, the creatorship (<s>nirmātṛtva</s>) and sovereignty (<s>īśvaratva</s>) [over] the manifestation of the universe [belong to Śiva alone].

children.text: ekaiva cānusaṃdhānāt $ sā proktā sarvasaṃvidām &
svasaṃvedanaparyāya- % mātṛtattvam anādi tat || 25 ||
children.translated_text: (verse 25cd) that beginningless principle (<s>tattva</s>) of the knower (<s>mātṛ</s>), synonymous with self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>).
(verse 25ab) And that [power] is declared to be one alone, through the continuous apprehension (<s>anusaṃdhāna</s>) of all cognitions —

children.text: Vṛ: saiśvarī parāśaktiḥ samastānāṃ vicchinnanīlāsisaṃvidāṃ saṃyojanaviyojanādau kārye pūrāparādikoṭāv aikyānusaṃdhānam āśritya tadādhārabhūtān avacchedinī ekaiva, tad eva svasaṃvedanaparyāyaṃ mātur anādi tattvam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That sovereign supreme power (<s>parāśakti</s>), relying upon the continuous apprehension of unity at the junctures of before and after etc. — in the work of joining and separating all the discrete cognitions of blue, a pot, etc. — is one alone, delimiting [them all] as their ground. And that very [thing] is declared as the beginningless principle of the knower, synonymous with self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>).

children.text: bhāvavyavasthā yan niṣṭhā $ tasyāhaṃbhāvabhāginaḥ &
vyāpitvam anusaṃdhānaṃ % taj jaḍasya na yujyate || 26 ||
children.translated_text: pervasiveness is [its] synthetic awareness — that is not possible for the insentient. (Verse 26)
The establishment of entities rests upon which [consciousness]; of that which partakes of I-consciousness,

children.text: Vṛ: yatra sarvārthānāṃ vyavasthitiḥ pratiṣṭhitā tasya saṃvidātmanaḥ pūrṇāhaṃtāparāmarśasārasyājaḍapramātuḥ svātantryāvinābhāvavattvāt sarvatrānusaṃdhānātmakaṃ vyāpitvam asti, tac cāsvatantrasya jaḍasya na ghaṭate vimarśasāratvābhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: Commentary: That in which the establishment of all objects is grounded — of that [knower] whose nature is <s>saṃvid</s> (consciousness), whose essence is the reflective awareness of full <s>ahaṃtā</s> (I-consciousness), i.e., the sentient knower (<s>ajaḍa-pramātṛ</s>) — because of the inseparability from autonomy (<s>svātantrya</s>), there is pervasiveness consisting of synthetic awareness (<s>anusaṃdhāna</s>) everywhere. And that is not possible for the insentient, which lacks autonomy, because of the absence of reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>) as its essence.

children.text: tato bhede tu bhāsasya $ ghaṭate bhāsamānatā &
tenoktam pratyabhijñāyāṃ % tadadvayamayaṃ jagat || 27 ||
children.translated_text: hence it is said in the <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>: "the universe consists of that non-dual [consciousness]." (Verse 27)
Therefore, in differentiation, the luminosity of manifestation is possible,

children.text: Vṛ: ajaḍatvam āśritya punar etāvati bhedollāsātmake viśvasmin nīlasukhāder bhāsasyāparikṣīṇāntaḥsthiter eva jñānaśaktyā bahirbhāsinaḥ prakāśamānatāyā ghaṭanāt; atha cābhedam avalambya jaḍasya punaḥ prakāśanopapatter anyathā tv aprakāśanāt | tena hetunā śrīmadīśvarapratyabhijñāyāṃ saṃvidadvayaprakṛti viśvam uktaṃ bhavatīti śivam ||
children.translated_text: Commentary: Taking recourse to sentience (<s>ajaḍatva</s>), in this entire universe whose nature is the manifestation of differentiation — since the luminosity of blue, pleasure, and so forth, whose inner abiding is undiminished, becomes manifest externally through the power of knowledge (<s>jñānaśakti</s>), [thus] its being luminous is possible. Moreover, taking recourse to non-duality, the manifestation of the insentient is also explained; otherwise there would be non-manifestation. For that reason, in the glorious <s>Īśvarapratyabhijñā</s>, the universe is said to be of the nature of non-dual consciousness (<s>saṃvidadvayaprakṛti</s>). <s>Śivam</s> (auspiciousness).

children.text: [pramātṛsiddhāv ācāryotpaladevakṛtau manāk |
children.translated_text: [In the <s>Pramātṛsiddhi</s> composed by the teacher <s>Utpaladeva</s>, briefly,

children.text: candrābdhyaṣṭenduśākābde śāstrī vṛttiṃ haro vyadhāt // [śāka era 1841]]
children.translated_text: in the <s>Śāka</s> year [1841], <s>Hara</s> the scholar composed the commentary.]

children.text: ity ajaḍapramātṛsiddhau śrīmānmahāmāheśvarācāryotpaladevapādaviracitāyāṃ vṛttiḥ samāptā ||
children.translated_text: Thus concludes the commentary on the <s>Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi</s>, composed by the glorious great <s>Māheśvara</s> teacher <s>Utpaladeva</s>.

children.text:
śrīmatpratāpabhūbhartur ājñayā prītaye satām |
madhusūdanakaulena saṃpādyeyaṃ prakāśitā//
children.translated_text: By the command of the illustrious king <s>Pratāpa</s>, for the delight of the virtuous, this [work
was edited and published by <s>Madhusūdana Kaula</s>.]
